version.changelog: Bundle source code: no git clone needed, all files included

llm.summary: The code mostly matches the stated Moodle connector purpose, but there are multiple inconsistencies (hard-coded default password, mismatched license/metadata, and SKILL.md vs code disagreements) that warrant caution before installing or supplying real credentials.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the included Python modules: a Moodle REST client, batch downloader, and an MCP server. Required packages (requests, cryptography, playwright, mcp) and behavior (OAuth to Microsoft, Moodle API, file downloads, caching) are coherent with a Moodle connector.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to set MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD in the MCP server config, but mcp_server.py does not read that env var — it constructs the connector with a hard-coded password ('test-pass'). The README also contains duplicate/conflicting license statements and repeated/truncated sections. mcp_server returns exception strings directly to MCP clients (server.call_tool), which may leak internal error text. Otherwise, instructions to run playwright and to copy a config template align with the code's behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but SKILL.md and package.json expect pip install -r requirements.txt and 'playwright install chromium' which will download browser binaries. That download is expected for Playwright-based SSO but increases attacker surface if run blindly. No remote/untrusted code URLs were used during static inspection.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but SKILL.md suggests supplying MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD for headless MCP use. The code does not honor that: mcp_server instantiates MoodleConnector with password='test-pass' and batch_downloader.py default password is 'test-pass' too. Hard-coded weak default passwords and the mismatch between documentation and code are disproportionate and risky — they can cause credential-decryption failures or accidental credential exposure if users assume the env var is used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes cache files and an encrypted credentials file (credentials.enc) in the skill directory, which is expected for a connector. It does not request always:true or change agent/global settings. Persistence is limited to its own files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement what it claims, but several red flags mean you should not run it against real accounts until verified: 1) The MCP example in SKILL.md tells you to set MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD, but mcp_server.py ignores env vars and uses the hard-coded password 'test-pass' — change that in the code before use. 2) Batch downloader and MCP server default to 'test-pass' (weak); pick a strong password and verify encrypt/decrypt works. 3) SKILL.md and package.json disagree about the license (MIT vs GPLv3); confirm licensing if that matters. 4) The code uses Playwright and suggests running 'playwright install chromium' which downloads browser binaries — run in a sandbox if you are cautious. 5) The MCP server returns raw exception strings; review/remove any logging or returns that might leak tokens. Recommended next steps: inspect the repository URL yourself, search the code for 'test-pass' and replace it with a secure handling of MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD (and make the code actually read the env var), run the skill in an isolated VM/container, and only provide non-production tokens for initial tests. If you want higher assurance, ask the author to fix the env-var/parameter mismatch and the license inconsistencies before using with real credentials.
